title: 📘 UNIT 1: HISTORY, HISTORIOGRAPHY, AND HUMAN EVOLUTION
notes: History → organized and critical study of the human past using evidence.

title: 1.1 📜 History and Historiography
notes:
History → study of past human events, thoughts and deeds based on interpretation of evidence.

The word History comes from Greek 'istoria' → inquiry or knowledge gained through investigation.

History studies → change, continuity, causes, consequences and human experiences.

title: 1.1.1 🔬 History as an Academic Discipline
notes:
History uses systematic methods, reliable evidence and critical analysis to study human societies.

It helps to:
• Understand the past.
• Understand present society.
• Learn from past achievements and mistakes.
• Develop identity.
• Analyze and solve social problems.

📌 History is considered a social science and has its own methodology.

title: 1.1.2 ✍️ Historiography
notes:
Historiography → history of historical writing and the methods used to research, interpret and write history.

👤 Herodotus → 'Father of History'.
👤 Thucydides → critical and chronological historical writing.
👤 Leopold von Ranke → 'Father of Modern Historiography'.

Key elements → sources + interpretation + presentation + objectivity + historical method.

title: 1.1.3 🇪🇹 Ethiopian Historiography
notes:
Ethiopia has an indigenous tradition of historical writing from the 14th century.

Major sources → chronicles and hagiographies.

👤 Job Ludolf → founded Ethiopian studies in Europe in the late 17th century and published the first modern history of Ethiopia in 1684.

1963 → Institute of Ethiopian Studies (IES) established, helping broaden Ethiopian studies beyond the north.

title: 1.1.4 📚 Sources of History
notes:
Primary sources → direct evidence from the period being studied.

Examples → monuments, inscriptions, coins, letters, diaries, memoirs, chronicles, contracts, photographs, films and eyewitness accounts.

Secondary sources → later interpretations or reconstructions of the past.
Example → most history books.

🗣️ Oral sources → can be primary or secondary depending on whether the information is firsthand or hearsay.

Source criticism → critically checking authenticity, meaning and reliability of evidence.

title: 1.1.5 ⚖️ Objectivity and Historical Writing
notes:
Objectivity → presenting historical evidence as accurately and fairly as possible without personal bias.

Historical writing process:
1. Collect evidence.
2. Critically examine sources.
3. Interpret evidence.
4. Present the history objectively.

⚠️ Complete objectivity is difficult, so historical accounts may be revised when new evidence appears.

title: 1.1.6 ⏳ Periodization in History
notes:
Periodization → dividing the human past into chronological periods to make history easier to study.

Human-behavior approach → Savagery → Barbarous → Civilization.

Tool-making approach → Stone Age → Bronze Age → Iron Age.

Economic approach → Hunting & Gathering → Farming & Animal Husbandry → Industrial Age.

title: 1.1.7 🕰️ Prehistory and History
notes:
Prehistory → period before the development of writing, traditionally around 4000 B.C.

History → period associated with written records.

Stone Age → roughly 2.5 million–5,000 B.P.

African history → Pre-colonial → Colonial → Post-colonial.

Ethiopian history → Ancient: c.1000 B.C–1270 A.D → Medieval: 1270–1855 → Modern: 1855–present.

title: 1.2 🧬 Origin of Human Beings
notes:
Human origins are studied mainly through archaeology, anthropology, fossils, artifacts and other scientific evidence.

Two major views:
• Creationist View → humans originated through supernatural/divine creation.
• Scientific View → humans developed through evolutionary processes over very long periods.

title: 1.2.1 🧠 Theories of Human Origin
notes:
Creationism → origin of humans and life explained through divine creation.

Evolution → simple forms of life gradually developed into more complex forms over millions of years.

👤 Charles Darwin → explained evolution and natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species' (1859).

Natural selection → organisms with advantageous traits are more likely to survive and reproduce.

title: 1.2.2 🦴 Hominids and Human Evolution
notes:
Hominids → human and human-like ancestors identified mainly through fossil evidence.

Major stages include:
• Australopithecines.
• Homo habilis → associated with early Oldowan tools.
• Homo erectus → associated with Acheulean tools; controlled fire and spread beyond Africa.
• Homo sapiens → modern human species.

📌 Africa provides major fossil evidence for human evolution.

title: 1.2.3 🪨 Early Cultural Developments
notes:
Stone Age → period when stone tools were the major technological tools.

Three stages:
• Paleolithic → Old Stone Age.
• Mesolithic → Middle Stone Age.
• Neolithic → New Stone Age.

Important Ethiopian sites → Gona, Afar, Omo, Konso-Gardula, Melka-Kunture and Gademotta.

title: 1.2.4 🪓 Paleolithic Period — Old Stone Age
notes:
Paleolithic → about 2.5 million–8,000 B.P.

People were mainly hunter-gatherers.

Major developments:
• Stone tools and weapons.
• Discovery and use of fire.
• Cave and rock-shelter occupation.
• Clothing from animal skins.
• Cave paintings.

Stages → Lower Paleolithic → Middle Paleolithic → Upper Paleolithic.

title: 1.2.5 🔨 Oldowan and Acheulean Tools
notes:
Oldowan → earliest simple stone-tool technology; made mainly by direct percussion/flaking.
👤 Associated with → Homo habilis.
📍 Ethiopia → Gona, Afar and Omo.

Acheulean → more advanced hand-axe technology; tools were bifacial and carefully shaped.
👤 Associated with → Homo erectus.
📍 Ethiopia → Konso-Gardula, Gedeb and Melka-Kunture.

title: 1.2.6 🏹 Middle and Upper Paleolithic
notes:
Middle Paleolithic → more refined and standardized tools; smaller flake tools became common.

Upper Paleolithic → standardized blades, microliths and composite tools became widespread.

Bone tools → increasingly used.

📌 Human biological and cultural development accelerated during this period.

title: 1.2.7 🌾 Neolithic Revolution
notes:
Neolithic Revolution → transition from hunting and gathering to food production through domestication of plants and animals.

Major effects:
• Agriculture developed.
• Permanent settlement increased.
• Population grew.
• Food surplus developed.
• Division of labour increased.
• Specialized occupations emerged.
• Larger and more complex societies developed.
• Helped create conditions for early states.

title: 1.2.8 🇪🇹 Neolithic Developments in Ethiopia
notes:
Evidence shows early agricultural and Neolithic developments in Ethiopia and the Horn.

Important developments → domestication of plants and animals + sedentary life + ceramics + grinding stones + polished axes.

Important crops → enset, teff, noog, finger millet and coffee.

📌 These developments contributed to the emergence of complex societies.

title: 1.3 🏛️ Emergence of State
notes:
Early states emerged from increasingly organized human communities such as families, clans and tribes.

The earliest known states appeared about 6,000 years ago.

State formation differed from society to society.

title: 1.3.1 🌾 Agriculture and State Formation
notes:
Agriculture → permanent settlement → food surplus → population growth → division of labour → social classes → organized government → early states.

📌 Food production and surplus were major foundations for the rise of early states, especially around river valleys.

title: 1.3.2 👑 Theories of the Emergence of State
notes:
Important factors proposed for state formation:
• Religion → religious authority helped legitimize political power.
• War → successful military leaders gained political control.
• Leadership → strong leaders organized and controlled communities.
• Trade → control of important trade routes increased wealth and power.
• Irrigation → management of water systems required organized authority.
• Agriculture → surplus food supported larger and more complex societies.

title: 1.3.3 ⛪ Divine Right Theory
notes:
Divine Right Theory → political authority was believed to come from God.

Kings were considered representatives or chosen rulers of the supreme deity.

📌 Religion could therefore combine religious and political authority and strengthen kingship.

notes:
